name: Creative & Media
summary: Image and music generation are mainstream, video is consolidating after Sora's exit, and the fight over training data is moving from lawsuits to settlements, licensing deals and labelling rules.

regions.name: Image & design
regions.summary: Image generation is built into chat apps, search and pro tools; Adobe is adding agents across Creative Cloud, while nonconsensual sexualized images draw regulator action.

landmarks.name: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image)
landmarks.summary: Google released its faster image model on 26 February with 4K output and made it the default in the Gemini app, Search AI Mode and Lens.

landmarks.name: Adobe Firefly AI Assistant
landmarks.summary: Adobe announced an agentic assistant that runs multi-step tasks across Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator and other apps; in-app public betas followed in June.

landmarks.name: Grok sexualized deepfake scandal
landmarks.summary: Grok on X produced undressed images of real people, including children; Ofcom opened a formal probe on 12 January, the EU followed, and Indonesia and Malaysia blocked it.

regions.whyItMatters: Image tools are where most people first meet generative AI, and where misuse against real people is most visible.
regions.openQuestion: Can safeguards and labelling keep pace with models that edit photos of real people on request?

regions.name: Video & film
regions.summary: Video models from Google and Chinese labs lead after OpenAI said it would shut Sora; studios use AI for effects shots while studio licensing deals remain unsettled.

landmarks.name: OpenAI discontinues Sora
landmarks.summary: OpenAI said on 24 March it would discontinue the Sora app and API; reports cite compute costs and a research pivot. Disney then dropped its planned deal.

landmarks.name: Disney and OpenAI $1B licensing deal
landmarks.summary: Disney agreed to license 200+ characters to Sora for three years and invest $1B in OpenAI; the deal was reportedly never completed before Sora was shut.

landmarks.name: Kling 3.0 launch
landmarks.summary: Kuaishou launched Kling Video 3.0 and 3.0 Omni with clips of up to 15 seconds and native audio in several languages, first for Ultra subscribers.

landmarks.name: Netflix uses generative AI in final footage
landmarks.summary: Netflix said 'The Eternaut' used generative AI for a building-collapse scene, its first use in final footage, finished about ten times faster than usual.

regions.whyItMatters: Video is the costliest media to generate, so it shows whether consumer generative AI can pay for its own compute.
regions.openQuestion: Will studios license characters and libraries to video models, or keep the tools in-house for effects work?

deepDives.title: Video generation models as world simulators
deepDives.why: How diffusion transformers generate video, in OpenAI's own technical note.

deepDives.title: Artificial Analysis
deepDives.why: Blind-vote arenas ranking text-to-video and image-to-video models.

deepDives.title: C2PA content credentials
deepDives.why: The provenance standard used to label generated and edited media.

regions.name: Music & audio
regions.summary: Major labels have moved from suing AI music generators to licensing them, while AI tracks flood streaming uploads and begin to appear on charts.

landmarks.name: Warner Music settles with Suno
landmarks.summary: WMG dropped its suit for a licensing deal; Suno said it would launch licensed models in 2026 and retire current ones.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked in this pass (search budget ran out); trade-press source, widely reported

landmarks.name: Universal settles with Udio
landmarks.summary: UMG settled and agreed a licensed AI music platform with Udio; download limits that followed angered existing Udio users.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked in this pass (search budget ran out); trade-press source, widely reported

landmarks.name: AI tracks pass half of Deezer uploads
landmarks.summary: Deezer said AI-generated tracks passed 50% of daily uploads for the first time, up from 44% in April, yet draw only 1 to 3% of streams.

regions.whyItMatters: Music is the first creative sector where rights holders and AI generators have moved from court to licensed products.
regions.openQuestion: Will licensed AI music pay artists meaningfully, and can streaming services contain the flood of uploads?

deepDives.title: Deezer newsroom: AI music share of uploads
deepDives.why: The only regular platform data on AI upload volumes, stream share and detection

deepDives.title: US Copyright Office: Copyright and AI
deepDives.why: The Office's multi-part report on digital replicas, copyrightability and training.

regions.name: Writing & publishing
regions.summary: AI-written books fill self-publishing platforms and dilute revenue per title, while publishers test licensing and authors win payouts over pirated training data.

landmarks.name: Anthropic $1.5B authors settlement approved
landmarks.summary: A US judge gave final approval to the largest copyright class settlement, about $3,000 per work for roughly 500,000 pirated books used by Anthropic.

landmarks.name: AI books reach 20% of Amazon self-publishing
landmarks.summary: Preprint on 14,419 self-published genre-fiction e-books finds about 20% have substantial AI text; revenue per selling book fell across most genres.
landmarks.note: arXiv ID 2607 = posted July 2026; wider press coverage followed in September

landmarks.name: HarperCollins AI training licence
landmarks.summary: HarperCollins offered nonfiction authors $2,500 per title for a three-year opt-in AI training licence; Bloomberg reported the buyer was Microsoft.

regions.whyItMatters: Books are the clearest test of what training data is worth and of how cheap AI text changes a market for human work.
regions.openQuestion: Will per-book licensing become standard, and can platforms stop AI titles from diluting author income?

regions.name: Games & interactive
regions.summary: About half of new Steam games now disclose generative AI, mostly small titles; world models generate explorable scenes but remain research prototypes.

landmarks.name: Google Project Genie
landmarks.summary: Experimental prototype built on the Genie 3 world model lets US Google AI Ultra subscribers generate and explore worlds from text or image prompts.

landmarks.name: Steam rewrites AI disclosure rules
landmarks.summary: Valve reworded its disclosure form to focus on AI-generated content that players see, not efficiency tools used behind the scenes in development.

landmarks.name: Nearly half of new Steam games disclose AI
landmarks.summary: A community analysis found 49.9% of October 2026 Steam releases disclosed AI content, up from 26.4% a year earlier and far more common among small titles.

landmarks.name: SAG-AFTRA game deal with AI consent rules
landmarks.summary: Members ratified the Interactive Media Agreement, ending the video game strike; it requires consent and disclosure for digital replicas of performers.

regions.whyItMatters: Games combine art, code, voice and live interaction, so they show how AI spreads through a whole production pipeline.
regions.openQuestion: Will players accept AI-made content in major releases, or will it stay concentrated in small titles?

deepDives.why: Data analysis of Steam AI disclosures over time, by game size and content type

regions.name: Creators, licensing & provenance
regions.summary: Courts are drawing narrow lines on training and fair use, EU labelling duties were set to apply from August 2026, and settlements and licensing deals are becoming the norm.

landmarks.name: Getty v Stability AI UK ruling
landmarks.summary: UK High Court rejected Getty's secondary copyright claim, finding Stable Diffusion holds no infringing copies; Getty won only narrow watermark trade mark points.

landmarks.name: EU code on labelling AI-generated content
landmarks.summary: The Commission published the final voluntary Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI content, to help meet AI Act Article 50 duties from 2 August 2026.

landmarks.name: Thomson Reuters v Ross upheld on appeal
landmarks.summary: Third Circuit held that training a legal search tool on Westlaw headnotes was not fair use, while leaving the question open for generative models.

regions.whyItMatters: How courts and regulators treat training data and labelling sets the terms on which every generative model is built and sold.
regions.openQuestion: Is training generative models on copyrighted work fair use, and who gets paid if it is not?
